newsitem.title: USA: U.S. space shuttle landing delayed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. space shuttle landing delayed.

text.p: Bad weather in Florida delayed the landing of the space shuttle Atlantis on Wednesday, which was to bring home U.S. astronaut John Blaha from the Russian space station Mir.
Atlantis was scheduled to touchdown at the Kennedy Space Centre around 7:47 a.m. EST (1247 GMT), but cloudy skies proved to be a problem.
"The first of the two landing opportunities was waved off because of a build up of broken decks of cloud," mission commentator Rob Navias said.
Touchdown was reset for 9:23 a.m. EST (1423 GMT), by which time forecasters believed the clouds would have dissipated under the warmth of the rising sun.
"Hopefully we'll get you down today sometime," mission control's Kevin Kregel had earlier radioed the astronauts.
Controllers in Houston said they were not considering a landing at the backup runway in California. The astronauts had enough supplies to remain in orbit until Friday if necessary.
The shuttle's 60-ft (18-meters) long clam-like payload bay doors were swung shut at about 4 a.m. EST (0900 GMT) in preparation for the planned landing.

Atlantis was to bring home John Blaha, who spent four months aboard Russia's Mir space station. The 54-year-old astronaut was to ride back to Earth in a reclining chair, his body wired with sensors so doctors could monitor his health as he felt the pull of gravity for the first time in 128 days.

Atlantis docked with Mir last week to collect Blaha and drop off his replacement, Jerry Linenger. The shuttle also delivered more than three tons of supplies and equipment to the 11-year-old space station.
